title: Probabilistic rubric and cohort-aware judge ensemble playbook for config/model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Current rollouts for config and model changes rely on deterministic pass/fail rubrics or single-LLM judges that produce brittle binary signals. This causes noisy rollout decisions, missed small regressions that are user-facing, and frequent false positives when distributional shifts occur across customer cohorts.

Objective: Define and implement a reproducible playbook that replaces brittle binary rubrics with probabilistic, per-criterion score distributions and a cohort-aware ensemble of LLM judges that are calibrated to produce well-calibrated confidence bands. The playbook should integrate with existing shadow-eval and rollout pipelines and produce clear telemetry, dashboarding, and automatic gating rules for canary/A-B rollouts.

Key deliverables: 
- A probabilistic rubric spec that maps judge outputs to calibrated probability distributions for each quality criterion (e.g., correctness, hallucination risk, safety-flag likelihood, style adherence).
- A judge-ensemble architecture spec: multiple judge prompts + model variants + statistical aggregation to produce mean, variance, and quantiles per criterion.
- Cohorting strategy: per-customer-type and per-prompt-cohort scoring, with cohort-specific baselines and bootstrapped uncertainty intervals.
- Calibration procedure: temperature-scaling and isotonic regression pipelines that run on held-out adjudicated datasets, producing calibration artifacts (calibration curves, ECE).
- Monitoring & gating rules: exact thresholds, expected false alarm rate, and sequential testing procedure (e.g., Bayesian sequential probability ratio test variant) for live rollouts.
- Implementation plan with telemetry naming, dashboards, PR template for config changes that include expected quality delta and CI.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce false-positive rollout halts due to eval noise by 40% within two months of adoption.
- Detect regressions with effect size >= 0.6 sigma in any primary cohort with 90% power at alpha=0.05 using the sequential test in the playbook.
- Calibration: expected calibration error (ECE) per criterion < 0.03 on internal adjudicated sets.

Design notes and constraints: 
- Should work with LLM-as-judge flow (judge can be an open model or Redwood-hosted model) and support multi-model ensembles (e.g., judge-v1 + judge-v2 + small deterministic heuristics).
- Must be computationally tractable to run in nightly shadow-eval and in fast rollouts (lightweight ensemble path + heavy offline calibration path).
- Cohorting must be configurable via eval config: fields like customer_tier, vertical, prompt_template_id, input_length_bucket.
- Outputs must be stored as time series with per-batch quantiles and bootstrap metadata to allow retrospective audits.

Implementation plan (high level): 
1) Spec and small prototype (2 weeks): define probabilistic rubric schema and produce a reference implementation that takes a list of judge logits/strings and returns per-criterion posteriors + ECE report.
2) Calibration harness (2 weeks): automated pipeline in evals infra that runs isotonic/temperature scaling per-criterion and emits artifacts to S3 + a metadata manifest.
3) Cohorting infra (2 weeks): add cohort keys in eval configs, implement stratified sampling and per-cohort metric aggregation.
4) Monitoring + gates (2 weeks): create dashboard panels, implement sequential testing module, and add rollout-gate integration to config rollout pipeline.
5) Rollout & docs (2 weeks): internal docs, PR templates, and training for SEs/PMs.

Telemetry & artifacts (naming):
- evals.prob_rubric.v1.{criterion}.{cohort}.mean -> daily time series of mean score
- evals.prob_rubric.v1.{criterion}.{cohort}.quantiles -> list of q10,q50,q90 strings
- evals.prob_rubric.v1.{criterion}.{cohort}.ece -> scalar calibration error
- evals.judge_ensemble.v1.{cohort}.member_logits -> stored per-eval for audit (retention subject to privacy policy)

Dashboards & alerts: 
- Dashboard: "ProbRubric Overview" with per-criterion, per-cohort trends, calibration curves, and ensemble disagreement heatmap.
- Alert: "Cohort Quality Drift" triggers when the posterior mean for any primary criterion drops below baseline by >0.4 sigma AND the lower 95% sequential CI exceeds the alarm threshold.

Rollout gating: 
- Canary stage only allowed if sequential test p-value > 0.05 for no-regression (one-sided test) across primary cohorts or if ensemble disagreement < 0.25 on average.
- If any high-severity cohort shows regression with posterior probability > 0.9, automatic rollback.

Data & adjudication: 
- Use existing juried adjudication sets (see PM-11012, PM-34111) to build calibration folds. Add a tiered adjudication plan for new prompt families used in a rollout.

Security & privacy considerations: ensure judge outputs stored respect PII redaction and retention policies. Calibration artifacts are non-PII but logs linking inputs to judge outputs are subject to customer data policy.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Ensemble size vs. cost: 3-judge ensemble (two LLM prompts + lightweight classifier) balances cost vs. variance reduction; we should validate diminishing returns.
- Choice of aggregator: Bayesian hierarchical pooling could borrow strength across cohorts but may mask cohort-specific regressions; prefer per-cohort baselines with optional hierarchical smoothing flagged in the dashboard.

Next steps: 
- PM to finalize spec (this ticket).
- Assign Eng owner to prototype judge-ensemble infra (follow-up ENG ticket).
- Set up a 2-week spike with applied-ml to validate ECE targets on representative adjudicated datasets.
